narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that Americans hold a negative view of the economy, believing it is hurting their families and favoring the wealthy.

units.meaning: 46% of responses fall in the 'economic conditions hurting' category.
accepted_routes: Just under half (46%) report economic conditions hurting
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 46% value must be visibly tied to the 'economic conditions hurting' category.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'roughly half ... hurting themselves and their families' narration clause
units.reviewer_question: Must the 46% hurting endpoint be a required headline number?

units.meaning: 54% of responses fall in the 'other' category, the complement to 'economic conditions hurting'.
accepted_routes: The remaining 54% is categorized as other
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 54% value must be visibly tied to the 'other' category.
units.temporal_anchor: the same 'roughly half' clause, showing the remainder/other portion
units.reviewer_question: Must the 54% other category be shown, or can the clip focus only on the hurting share?

units.meaning: The 'other' category is 8 percentage points larger than the 'economic conditions hurting' category (54% vs 46%).
accepted_routes: Other exceeds hurting by 8 percentage points
The hurting share is 8 points below other
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both 46% and 54% must be visible in the same comparison so the 8-point gap can be read.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'roughly half' clause when the hurting share is compared with other responses
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip explicitly state the 8-point gap, or is showing both values enough?

units.meaning: The displayed responses split 46% 'economic conditions hurting' and 54% 'other', together making 100%.
accepted_routes: The split is 46% hurting to 54% other
Together the two categories sum to 100%
Hurting and other account for 46% and 54% respectively
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both 46% and 54% must be visible as parts of the same two-category distribution.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'roughly half' clause where the response split is established
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip present both categories as a complete 46/54 split?

units.meaning: The 'economic conditions hurting' share is below the midpoint of the two-category split, i.e., just under half (46% vs 50% midpoint).
accepted_routes: The hurting share falls below a 50% midpoint
units.visual_evidence_rule: The viewer must be able to see that the 46% hurting value is below a 50% midpoint, either via a reference or explicit under-half statement.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'roughly half' clause, clarifying it is below half/majority
units.reviewer_question: Should the clip explicitly say the hurting share is below half/majority, or is that optional context?

optional_valid: Describing 'other' as the remainder/complement of the hurting share, without implying what it contains.
Using the relative_value framing (0.46 vs 0.54) as a size/order comparison rather than percentages.
Noting that the hurting share is close to half but not a majority.
unsupported_to_avoid: Americans believe the economy favors the wealthy or hurts poor/middle-class people
About a quarter of Americans said there was the right amount of economic inequality
A majority of Americans said the economy was helping the wealthy and hurting poor/middle-class people
The economy is actually not working
Any breakdown of the 54% 'other' category, such as right-amount, helping, or no opinion
Causal claims that economic conditions are causing harm
Any claim that 46% is a majority or that most Americans hold this view
notes: The table contains only a 46% 'economic conditions hurting' share and a 54% 'other' share, so all candidate units stay within that two-category split. The narration's wealthy/poor/middle-class and inequality claims are not in the table and are listed as unsupported.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
